extracted.intended_audience: general readers, students of comedy, and comedians seeking a taxonomy of comedic genres
extracted.subtask_description: Provide a taxonomy and short descriptions of comedic genres based on source of humor, delivery method, and context; lists notable examples for each genre. Useful for learning, classification, or selecting styles for performance or study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggressive Humour
rubrics_metrics.description: Insensitive to audience sentiment by igniting criticism and ridicule on subjects like racism, sexism or anything hurtful; differs from blue humor or dark comedy as it inclines more towards being humorous than being offensive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notable examples: Daniel Tosh, Brendon Burns, Anthony Jeselnik, Kunal Kamra, Bill Burr, Sarah Silverman, Paul Mooney, Don Rickles, Rufus Hound, George Carlin, Gianmarco Soresi, Bill Hicks, Ricky Gervais, Doug Stanhope, Frankie Boyle, Roseanne Barr, Jon Stewart, Brad Garrett, Denis Leary, Chris Morris, Kelsey Grammer, Patton Oswalt, Ari Shaffir, Lisa Lampanelli, Ian Cognito.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative comedy
rubrics_metrics.description: Differs from traditional punchline jokes; features many other forms such as observation, satire, surrealism, slapstick and improvisation. Emerged as a counter to establishment entertainment and disregarded established comedic movements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notable examples: Tony Allen, Alexei Sayle, Mark Steel, Dan Harmon, Dave Gorman, Linda Smith, Jeremy Hardy, Ron Sparks, Alan Davies, Ben Elton, Jo Brand, Stewart Lee, Sean Hughes, Rik Mayall, Adrian Edmondson, Malcolm Hardee, Kristen Schaal, Kelsey Grammer, Kevin McAleer, Simon Munnery, Arthur Smith, Arnold Brown, Robert Newman, Kevin Eldon, James Acaster, Kenny Sebastian, Hannah Gadsby.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anecdotal comedy
rubrics_metrics.description: Named after Greek term for anecdote; personal stories that may be true or partly true but embellished.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notable examples: Kevin Hart, Louis C.K., Patrice O'Neal, Russell Peters, Aries Spears, Hannibal Buress, Deon Cole, John Mulaney, Bill Burr, Roy Wood Jr., Michael McIntyre, Dave Chappelle, Cedric the Entertainer, Bernie Mac, Gabriel Iglesias, Alonzo Bodden, D. L. Hughley, Jamie Foxx, Peter Kay, Eddie Griffin, Brad Williams, Hasan Minhaj, Patton Oswalt, Jim Carrey, Jim Gaffigan, Tom Segura, Biswa Kalyan Rath, Colin Jost, Trevor Noah, Daniel Kitson, Danny Baker, Romesh Ranganathan, Chris Rock, Zakir Khan, Hiroyuki Miyasako, Theo Von, Annie Lederman, Wanda Sykes, Kathleen Madigan, Tig Notaro, Chris D'Elia, Jack Whitehall, Kanan Gill, Roseanne Barr.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anti-humor
rubrics_metrics.description: Indirect humor derived from the comedian delivering something intentionally not funny or lacking intrinsic meaning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notable examples: Andy Kaufman, Andy Samberg, Norm Macdonald, Ted Chippington, John Thomson, Andy Milonakis, Neil Hamburger, Tim & Eric, Eric Andre, Will Ferrell, Edward Aczel, Paul Putner, Richard Herring, Albert Brooks, Steve Martin, Martin Mull, Bill Bailey, Noel Fielding, Mark Silcox, Perry Farrel, Nogla, Beetlejuice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Black comedy (dark comedy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Deals with disturbing subjects such as death, drugs, terrorism, rape, and war; sometimes related to the horror genre. Often said to be said by a disliked character.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notable examples: Jim Norton, Lenny Bruce, Bill Hicks, Dave Chappelle, Frankie Boyle, Jimmy Carr, Louis C.K., Kevin Smith, Denis Leary, Dennis Miller, Monty Python, Richard Pryor, Ricky Gervais, George Carlin, Chris Rush, Jim Jefferies, Mike Ward, Penn & Teller, Norm Macdonald, Christopher Titus, Sacha Baron Cohen, Trey Parker/Matt Stone, Howard Stern, Quentin Tarantino, David Cross, Judah Friedlander, Pete Davidson, Anthony Jeselnik, Daniel Tosh, Seth Rogen/Evan Goldberg, Bobcat Goldthwait, Brendon Burns, Mark Normand, Jerrod Carmichael, Fin Taylor, Dr. Strangelove, Chris Dangerfield, PFFR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blue comedy
rubrics_metrics.description: Typically sexual in nature (risqué) and/or using profanity; sometimes using gender- or race-based humor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notable examples: Samay Raina, Joan Rivers, Dave Attell, Roy 'Chubby' Brown, Frankie Boyle, Jimmy Carr, Dave Chappelle, Cheech & Chong, Jim Davidson, Derek and Clive, Geoffrey Chaucer, Michael Che, Billy Connolly, Jenny Eclair, The Firesign Theatre, Redd Foxx, Jason Biggs, Shane Gillis, Lisa Lampanelli, Martin Lawrence, George Lopez, Bernard Manning, Monty Python, Eddie Murphy, Chris Rock, Joe Rogan, Bob Saget, Sarah Silverman, Frank Skinner, Doug Stanhope, Robert Schimmel, Amy Schumer, John Valby, Ron White, Felicia Michaels, William Shakespeare.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burlesque
rubrics_metrics.description: Nonsensical or ridiculous treatment of serious works of art, music, literature or theatre to make a statement in a humorous and entertaining way; prior knowledge of the subject is required by the audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notable examples/works: Burlesque, The Play That Goes Wrong, A Modest Proposal, The Rehearsal, Beggar's Opera, The Rape of the Lock, Morgante, O Brother, Where Art Thou?.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character comedy
rubrics_metrics.description: Derived from a persona invented by the performer, often stereotypical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notable examples: Phyllis Diller, Andy Kaufman, Jim Carrey, Wallace Shawn, Bob Nelson, Catherine Tate, Paul Eddington, Andrew Dice Clay, Rich Hall, Tim Allen, John Gordon Sinclair, Lenny Henry, Sacha Baron Cohen, Christopher Ryan, Billy West, Steve Guttenberg, Jeff Bergman, Jerry Sadowitz, Steve Coogan, Fred Armisen, Jay London, Larry the Cable Guy, Adam Sandler, Pete Davidson, Steve Carell, Richard Kind, Maurice LaMarche, Martin Short, Rainn Wilson, Jim Varney, Sarah Silverman, Paul Reubens, Rob Brydon, Rowan Atkinson, Gabriel Iglesias, Peter Helliar, Harry Enfield, Margaret Cho, Matt Lucas/David Walliams, Stephen Colbert, Al Murray, Paul Whitehouse, Charlie Higson, Kevin Hart, Jack Black, Alex Borstein, Leigh Francis, Barry Humphries, Paul O'Grady, Caroline Aherne, Kelsey Grammer, Eric Bauza, Kristen Wiig, Andy Lauer, Kate Berlant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cringe comedy
rubrics_metrics.description: A comedy of embarrassment derived from inappropriate actions or words; popular in television shows and film, but occasionally in stand-up.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notable examples: Steve Carell, Stephen Colbert, Ricky Gervais, Stephen Merchant, Richard Herring, Ben Stiller, Larry David, Steve Coogan, Bob Saget, Nathan Fielder. TV shows: The Office, Curb Your Enthusiasm, Peep Show, People Just Do Nothing, The Larry Sanders Show, Ally McBeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadpan comedy
rubrics_metrics.description: Not strictly a style of comedy; telling jokes without a change in facial expression or change of emotion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notable examples: Pat Paulsen, Dennis Allen, Milton Jones, Jack Dee, Bob Newhart, Jimmy Carr, Steven Wright, Peter Cook, Stephen Colbert, Craig Ferguson, Dylan Moran, Tig Notaro, Karl Pilkington, Nate Bargatze, Richard Ayoade, W. Kamau Bell, Buster Keaton, Bill Murray, Marc Evan Jackson, Jim Gaffigan, Les Dawson, Paul Merton, Mike Birbiglia, Mitch Hedberg, Bruce McCulloch, Demetri Martin, Todd Barry, Elliott Goblet, Aubrey Plaza, Zach Galifianakis, Michael Longfellow, Michael Redmond, Judah Friedlander, James Acaster, Richard Belzer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Heritage comedy
rubrics_metrics.description: The comedian discusses humorous traits or stereotypes about their own culture or heritage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notable examples: Pat Cooper, Bill Engvall, Jeff Foxworthy, Alex Edelman, Johnny Hardwick, Gabriel Iglesias, Eddie Murphy, Marcello Hernández, Trevor Noah, George Lopez, Jackie Mason, Russell Peters, Richard Pryor, Yakov Smirnoff, Henning Wehn, Nigel Ng, Jarlath Regan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improvisational comedy
rubrics_metrics.description: Largely unplanned routines, often featured on television shows such as Curb Your Enthusiasm and Whose Line Is It Anyway?.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notable examples: Robin Williams, Jonathan Winters, Joan Rivers, Eddie Izzard, Bob Nelson, Paula Poundstone, Paul Merton, Abish Mathew, Tony Slattery, Josie Lawrence, Jim Sweeney, Steve Steen, Lily Tomlin, Wayne Brady, Ryan Stiles, Colin Mochrie, Drew Carey, Greg Proops, John Sessions, Neil Mullarkey, Kathy Greenwood, Brad Sherwood, Charles Esten, Jeff B. Davis, Tina Fey, Amy Poehler, Stephen Colbert, Jonathan Mangum, Mark Meer, Larry David, Peter Kay, Johnny Vegas, Dave Lawrence, Paul Spence, John Valby, Kaneez Surka.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inside humor
rubrics_metrics.description: Requires special knowledge in order to be appreciated by the audience (references not broadly known).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example from page: The Firesign Theatre quoted lyrics and parodied character names from Beatles albums and created self-referential inside jokes across albums.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insult comedy
rubrics_metrics.description: Offensive insults directed at the audience or other performers, usually in response to audience hecklers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notable examples: Don Rickles, Andrew Dice Clay, Ricky Gervais, Bob Saget, Frankie Boyle, Jimmy Carr, Jerry Sadowitz, Sam Kinison, Santhanam, Al Murray, Triumph the Insult Comic Dog, Joan Rivers, Bianca Del Rio, Roy 'Chubby' Brown, Marcus Valerius Martialis, Norm Macdonald, Jonathan Ross, Jeffrey Ross, Dave Attell, Lisa Lampanelli, D.L. Hughley, Greg Giraldo, Goundamani, Kathy Griffin, John Valby, Gilbert Gottfried, Harry Hill, Daniel Tosh. Note: Don Rickles famously built his career on insult comedy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mockumentary
rubrics_metrics.description: Parody using the conventions of documentary style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notable works: Fubar & Fubar 2, Borat, This Country, This Is Spinal Tap, The Monkees, The Rutles, Summer Heights High, Electric Apricot: Quest for Festeroo, The Office, Brüno, Parks and Recreation, Modern Family, Come Fly with Me, Angry Boys, The Compleat Al, Trailer Park Boys, What We Do in the Shadows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Musical comedy
rubrics_metrics.description: Derived from music with or sometimes without lyrics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notable examples/artists: Pink Guy, Rucka Rucka Ali, Bill Bailey, Denis Leary, Tim Minchin, Ninja Sex Party, The Lonely Island, Fred Armisen, Flight Of The Conchords, Les Luthiers, Mitch Benn, Tenacious D, Spinal Tap, Stephen Lynch, Eminem, 'Weird Al' Yankovic, Bob Rivers, Bo Burnham, Wayne Brady, the Bonzo Dog Doo-Dah Band, Tiny Meat Gang, Tom Lehrer, Steve Martin, Victor Borge, Jack Douglass, The Axis of Awesome, John Valby, Seth MacFarlane, Jasper Carrott, Boothby Graffoe, David O'Doherty, Rachel Bloom, Adam Sandler, Allan Sherman, Mike Myers, Eddie Murphy, Carlos Alazraqui, Chris Rock, Kevin Hart, Pete Seeger, Robin Williams, Peter Schickele, Victoria Wood, Jon Lajoie, Dan Bull, Da Vinci's Notebook, Danny Gonzalez, Flo and Joan, Spike Jones and His City Slickers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observational comedy
rubrics_metrics.description: Pokes fun at everyday life, often by inflating the importance of trivial things or by observing the silliness of social conventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notable examples: George Carlin, Cheech & Chong, Jerry Seinfeld, Louis C.K., Bobby Lee, Amy Schumer, Craig Ferguson, Larry David, Ken Jeong, Mitch Hedberg, Billy Connolly, Michael McIntyre, Russell Howard, Colin Jost, Cedric the Entertainer, Steve Harvey, Micky Flanagan, Brad Williams, Gabriel Iglesias, Gianmarco Soresi, W. Kamau Bell, Matt Groening, Ray Romano, Chris Rush, Dane Cook, Seann Walsh, Pete Davidson, Chris Rock, Jim Gaffigan, Kathy Greenwood, Ellen DeGeneres, Russell Peters, John Mulaney, Peter Kay, Victoria Wood, Jack Whitehall, Kanan Gill, Richard Belzer, Mark Normand, Anubhav Singh Bassi.

rubrics_metrics.name: One-line joke
rubrics_metrics.description: A joke delivered in a single line. A good one-liner is pithy (concise and meaningful).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notable examples: Tim Allen, Tommy Cooper, Rodney Dangerfield, Ken Dodd, Stewart Francis, Milton Jones, Tim Vine, Lee Mack, Henny Youngman, Mitch Hedberg, Sean Hegarty, Mick Miller, Jimmy Carr, Steven Wright, Demetri Martin, Anthony Jeselnik, Doug Benson, Jim Gaffigan, Zach Galifianakis, Shappi Khorsandi, Dan Mintz, Groucho Marx, Jay London, Mark Normand, Mark Simmons, Ahren Belisle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical comedy
rubrics_metrics.description: Similar to slapstick; uses physical movement and gestures, often influenced by clowning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notable examples: Tim Allen, Johnny Knoxville, Michael Richards, Charlie Chaplin, Buster Keaton, Jacques Tati, Jim Carrey, Bob Nelson, Norman Wisdom, Jerry Lewis, Robin Williams, Chevy Chase, John Ritter, Conan O'Brien, Kunal Nayyar, Jason Lee, Mr. Bean, Michael Mcintyre, Lee Evans, Bill Irwin, David Shiner, Dick Van Dyke, Max Wall, John Belushi, Brent Butt, Kathy Greenwood, The Three Stooges, Lano & Woodley, Lucille Ball, Chris Farley, Sebastian Maniscalco, The Dangerous Brothers, Danny Kaye, Andy Lauer, Luke Rollason, Jordan Brookes, Jimeoin.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical jokes (pranking/trolling)
rubrics_metrics.description: Humor based around tricks being played on a person or group, causing embarrassment, perplexity, confusion, discomfort, or irritation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notable acts/shows: VanossGaming, SeaNanners, The Jerky Boys, Chop & Steele. Example film: Windy City Heat (2003 Comedy Central TV movie). TV shows: The Eric Andre Show, The Jamie Kennedy Experiment, Trigger Happy TV.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prop comedy
rubrics_metrics.description: Relies on ridiculous props, casual jackets or everyday objects used in humorous ways.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notable examples: Babatunde Omidina, Bob Nelson, Carrot Top, Gallagher, Timmy Mallett, The Amazing Johnathan, Jerry Sadowitz, Tape Face, Howie Mandel, Tommy Cooper, Harpo Marx, Bruce Baum, Sam Simmons, Spencer Jones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Screwball comedy
rubrics_metrics.description: A genre that emerged in the 1930s and 1940s; characterized by fast-paced, witty dialogue, farcical situations, and romantic storylines that often involve a battle of the sexes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notable performers/actors: Jean Arthur, Irene Dunne, Cary Grant, Edward Everett Horton, Carole Lombard, Fred MacMurray, William Powell, Rosalind Russell, Ralph Bellamy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shock humor
rubrics_metrics.description: A style of comedy that uses shock value to invoke a strong negative emotion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notable examples: Andrew Dice Clay, Howard Stern, Impractical Jokers, South Park, Jackass, Eric Andre, Andy Dick, Tom Green.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sitcom
rubrics_metrics.description: Television series with scripted dialogue set in a thematic situation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notable examples: Seinfeld, Cheers, Drake & Josh, Fawlty Towers, Curb Your Enthusiasm, Ted Lasso, Black Books, Porridge, Dad's Army, Blackadder, Gavin & Stacey, The Royle Family, Brooklyn Nine-Nine, My Wife and Kids, Friends, NewsRadio, Taxi, Here We Go, The Office, Not Going Out, The Simpsons, Open All Hours, Only Fools and Horses, Benidorm, Dinner Ladies, Modern Family, Schmigadoon!, Two and a Half Men, Miranda, All in the Family, The Fresh Prince of Bel-Air, Family Guy, Parks and Recreation, South Park, The Good Place, How I Met Your Mother.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sketch
rubrics_metrics.description: A short scene on television or standup, similar to the sitcom; practised and typically performed live. Sketches sometimes spawn sitcom series.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notable performers/groups and shows: Armstrong and Miller, Cheech & Chong, Jennifer Saunders, Lorne Michaels, Dawn French, Craig Ferguson, Ryan Higa, Jack Douglass, Catherine Tate. TV shows: Monty Python, Armstrong and Miller, The Carol Burnett Show, The Jackie Gleason Show, Saturday Night Live, Studio C, Chappelle's Show, Firesign Theatre, In Living Color, A Bit of Fry & Laurie, Mad TV, Mr. Show, Tim and Eric Awesome Show, Great Job!, Wonder Showzen, Key & Peele, Lenny Henry, Little Britain, The Kapil Sharma Show, Million Dollar Extreme Presents: World Peace, The Whitest Kids U' Know.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spoof / Parody
rubrics_metrics.description: Humorous recreation of a book, film or play, either to pay homage or to ridicule the original.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notable examples/creators: Mel Brooks, Joe Alaskey, French and Saunders, Mitchell and Webb, I'm Sorry I Haven't a Clue, Dom Joly, Peter Serafinowicz, Matt Groening, Weird Al Yankovic, C.S Amudhan, Zucker, Abrahams and Zucker. Films and TV shows: Airplane!, Family Guy, Shriek, Look Around You, Onion News Network.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surreal comedy
rubrics_metrics.description: Based on bizarre juxtapositions, absurd situations, and nonsense logic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notable examples: Filthy Frank, Spike Milligan, Jay Kogen, Eddie Izzard, J. Stewart Burns, Ross Noble, Bill Bailey, Brent Butt, The Mighty Boosh, Steven Wright, Eric Andre, Russell Brand, Monty Python, Seth MacFarlane, David X. Cohen, Vic and Bob, The Goodies, Jack Handey, Derek Drymon, Wallace Wolodarsky, Harry Hill, The Kids in the Hall, Conan O'Brien, Tim and Eric, Paul Merton, Mitch Hedberg, Firesign Theatre, Shaun Micallef, Emo Philips, Hans Teeuwen, Tony Law, Chic Murray, VanossGaming, Brandon Rogers, Charlie Chuck, Trevor Lock, Sam Hyde/Million Dollar Extreme, The Good Place.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topical comedy / Satire
rubrics_metrics.description: Relies on news headlines and current affairs; dates quickly, but is popular for late night talk-variety shows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notable examples: Aristophanes, George Carlin, Cheech & Chong, Bill Hicks, Dick Gregory, Chris Morris, Dennis Miller, Norm Macdonald, Conan O'Brien, Russell Howard, Craig Ferguson, David Letterman, Jay Leno, Tom Lehrer, Dan Harmon, Andy Hamilton, Dave Allen, Bill Maher, Jon Stewart, Trevor Noah, Mark Twain, John Oliver, Ian Hislop, Brent Butt, Gianmarco Soresi, Paul Merton, Mort Sahl, Kathy Griffin, Stephen Colbert, Stewart Lee, Mark Thomas, Matt Groening, Rory Bremner, Howard Stern, W. Kamau Bell, Ben Elton, David Cross, Lewis Black, Pete Seeger, Chris Rock, Dave Chappelle, The Chaser, Punt and Dennis, Jon Holmes, Tanmay Bhat, Richard Belzer, Hari Kondabolu, Tim Dillon. TV and radio: The Daily Show, The Onion, The Babylon Bee, Have I Got News For You, Mock The Week, The News Quiz, Saturday Night Live, The Simpsons, The Tonight Show, Late Show with David Letterman, Wait Wait... Don't Tell Me!, South Park.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ventriloquism
rubrics_metrics.description: Involves character comedy; the comedian uses ventriloquy to 'throw' his or her voice into a dummy or puppet character. The ventriloquist generally speaks as the 'straight man' and gives comic lines to the dummy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notable examples: Fred Russell, Arthur Prince, Keith Harris, The Great Lester, Edgar Bergen, Paul Winchell, Jimmy Nelson, Shari Lewis, Señor Wences, Willie Tyler, Nina Conti, Darci Lynne, Jeff Dunham. Note: ventriloquists appealed historically to general audiences and children until some began using blue comedy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wit / Word play
rubrics_metrics.description: More intellectual forms based on clever, often subtle manipulation of language (though puns can be crude and farcical).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notable examples: Groucho Marx, William Shakespeare, Harry Hill, Jay Jason, Oscar Wilde, Woody Allen, George Carlin, Tim Vine, Stephen Fry, Demetri Martin, Bo Burnham, Firesign Theatre, Myq Kaplan, Crazy Mohan, Bugs Bunny, Ronnie Barker, Stanley Unwin.
